MXML Guide

MXML is an XML-based markup language used to create MelonUI pages. It describes the same elements, properties and callbacks that you use when building the UI in C#.

Page Structure

The root element must be MUIPage. You can set MxmlVersion="1" to explicitly select the language version; unsupported versions fail compilation.

Core types in MelonUI.Base and MelonUI.Default are available without namespace declarations. Attributes set public CLR properties. Normal XML escaping applies, such as &amp; for an ampersand and &#10; for a line break inside an attribute.

Compiling a Page

Register any application objects that the markup uses, then compile the file:

BackendObjects refers to existing objects that your application owns. The compiler does not dispose those objects. Backends declared in markup with Backends="Alias=TypeName" are created when needed and are owned by their page scope. A disposable backend created this way is cleaned up after failure, replacement or final page disposal.

Child pages inherit the available aliases. New declarations remain inside the child scope. Static backend classes can also be referenced without constructing an instance.

Children and Property Elements

UI elements belong to the element containing them, in declaration order. Data objects such as MenuItem and WorkItem go inside an explicit collection property instead of Children.

Property elements use Owner.Property, where Owner is the current type or one of its base types. Collections can contain one or more objects. A scalar property element can contain text or a binding.

Including Other Pages

Relative includes are resolved beside the file containing them. Attributes on the include element override settings from the included page. MXMLFilePath is also accepted as an include alias.

Compile(text, sourcePath) compiles the text you supply without rereading the file. sourcePath provides the directory used for relative includes. Without a source path, CompilerOptions.BaseDirectory is used, followed by the process working directory. Compiling never changes that working directory.

Recursive includes and documents exceeding the configured size/depth limits are reported as errors.

Element Names

Names must be unique within the nearest page, including ordinary nested containers. A nested MUIPage creates a new scope.

  • Name: Looks for an element inside the current page scope.
  • Settings/Name: Looks for Name inside the named Settings child page.
  • .: Refers to the current page.

Action targets can refer to elements declared later in the file. They are resolved after the page has been parsed.

Custom Types and Constructors

Normally the compiler uses a public parameterless constructor. You can register a factory when a type needs constructor arguments or services from the application. The factory must return a new, unattached and undisposed instance of the requested type.

Assemblies, Namespaces and Backends declarations in MXML are handled in phases, so their attribute order does not matter. Fully qualified names or CLR XML namespace prefixes can be used when short type names would be ambiguous.

Reloading MXML

The compiler builds a new page before replacing the current one. This allows an application to keep showing a working UI while a file is being edited:

  • Compilation Fails: The current children, root settings, bindings and focus are kept. Read the diagnostics to show the error.
  • Compilation Succeeds: Children are replaced and the old owned elements and bindings are disposed. A uniquely named eligible focus target is restored.
  • Root Properties: Properties included in the new markup replace their previous values. Omitted root settings remain unchanged.

While the window is running, compile on the UI thread using Post or InvokeAsync. Read the file outside that action. Custom setters and lifetime methods should not throw or cause external changes during compilation; normal rollback cannot undo arbitrary application behavior.

Notes

MXML is intended for trusted application and plugin code. It can create registered classes, call backends and include local files, so it should not be treated as a sandbox for untrusted input. DTDs and external XML entities are prohibited.

See Data Binding, MXML Actions, and Diagnostics and Troubleshooting for more information.
